*Circumcircle of $DEF$.* Its center is $O=\bigl(\tfrac{1-d}{2},\tfrac{\sqrt3(3d-1)}6\bigr)$ and its radius squared is $r^2=d^2-d+\tfrac13$.

*Radical axis $\ell$.* Subtracting the two circle equations gives $\ell:(d+1)x+\sqrt3(1-d)y=1$. Intersecting with line $BC:\;y=\sqrt3(1-x)$ yields
$$P=\left(\frac{3d-2}{2(2d-1)},\;\frac{\sqrt3\,d}{2(2d-1)}\right).$$

*Point $Q$.* The locus $\angle AQB=120^\circ$ is the minor arc $AB$ of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ (center $(\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{6})$, radius $\tfrac{\sqrt3}{3}$). $$|QO|^2=d^2-d+\tfrac13=r^2,$$

Restricted to the sampling interval $(0,\tfrac12)$, the favorable set is $(\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$ of length $\tfrac16$ out of total length $\tfrac12$. Hence the probability is $\tfrac{1/6}{1/2}=\tfrac13$.
